name: prd-taskmaster
conclusion_quantitative: prd-taskmaster (Ask) specifies 4 of 5 categories: 2 autonomy limits, 3 clarification rules, 4 approval gates, 10+ validation rules; none for escalation rules. Strongest: validation rules.
conclusion_qualitative: prd-taskmaster generates a comprehensive product requirements document with no deferred scope, publishes it as a GitHub issue and triggers a spec-shaping skill for execution. It front-loads clarification, asking discovery questions one at a time, and confirms the detected scope and any auto-fixes with the user. It runs 14 automated quality checks on the document and works with a fixed tool set. It sets no rules for handling failure.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_quantitative: 2 autonomy limits (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly frontmatter.
autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: There are 2 rules, both strict, 1 tied to a situation, evenly split between front matter and bullet points. The front matter limits the agent to `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Bash`, `AskUserQuestion` and `Skill`. When the user gives minimal answers, the agent uses its best guesses and documents the assumptions instead of asking more.

statements.quote: allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash, AskUserQuestion, Skill
If user provides minimal answers, use best guesses and document assumptions

clarification_rules.conclusion_quantitative: 3 clarification rules (3 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly prose.
clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: There are 3 rules, all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly running text. Clarifying questions come first, before execution. The agent asks the discovery questions interactively through `AskUserQuestion`, one at a time, but never asks about timelines as a way to cut scope.

statements.quote: Clarifying questions and pre-reqs come first, then execution runs to completion.
Ask questions interactively using AskUserQuestion. One question at a time.
**NEVER ask about timeline expectations as a way to reduce scope** — everything is must-deliver

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 4 approval gates (4 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, all strict, 1 tied to a situation, mostly running text. The agent confirms the auto-detected engineering scope (iOS, backend, cloud infrastructure) with the user through `AskUserQuestion`, and when it auto-fixes deferred items flagged by validation it asks the user to confirm.

statements.quote: **Detect Scope** — Auto-detect iOS / Backend / GCP-Infra from PRD + repo, confirm with user
**If validation fails on deferral checks:** Auto-fix by promoting deferred items to requirements or removing them entirely. Ask user to confirm.
Auto-detect from PRD content + repo structure, then confirm with user.

validation.conclusion_quantitative: 10+ validation rules (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
validation.conclusion_qualitative: There are 10 or more rules (the first 10 are kept), all strict, none tied to a situation, mostly bullet points. The agent validates the PRD with 14 automated checks, including an executive summary, a problem statement with user and business impact, SMART goals, at least 3 acceptance criteria per user story, testable must-priority requirements and numbered requirements.

statements.quote: Problem statement includes user AND business impact
User stories have acceptance criteria (minimum 3 per story)
All functional requirements are testable (not vague)
All requirements are Must priority (no Should/Could)

escalation.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent what to do when something goes wrong, such as stopping or reporting an error to the user.
